answer: Because the walnut stake is held until the relic settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the wharf audit lists each exposure. A farm running 76 keys thus forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. An attester must stake 26% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
